title: Runlog shared tables (schema version 1)

kind.description: What this document is. A pack says nothing; this says `tables`.

schemaVersion.description: The format's major version, as a pack carries one.

version.description: Semantic version. Entries changing changes this, or nobody holding it is offered the new ones.

description.description: What is in it, and who it is for.

defaultVariant.description: The variant used when a pack or a run does not name one.

title.description: What this pitch of the table is called, where somebody is choosing between them.

description.description: Who it is for and how hard it is, in a line.

roll.description: What is rolled. The entries must cover its whole range, as in a pack's own table.

id.description: Unique within this table. Referenced by saved runs, so avoid renaming.

title.description: Short heading, when the entry has a name of its own.

text.description: The rules text shown to the player, verbatim. This is what they read and obey.

on.description: The lifecycle point at which this fires.

do.description: Actions to run, in order, when it fires.

when.description: Only fire if every one of these still holds at trigger time.

label.description: How the pending obligation is described to the player.

items.description: Behavior attached to a result, optionally deferred to a later point in the unit or run.

requires.description: Conditions that must ALL hold for this result to make sense. When one fails the dice are thrown again, up to a few times, the way they are for a result the run lacks a requirement for. Use it where a result has no referent yet rather than where it is merely hard: `unitIndex: { gte: 2 }` on a result that sends somebody back to where the last one started. Note the asymmetry these games insist on: impossibility justifies a re-roll, difficulty never does.

grants.description: States applied to the relevant subject on resolution. Shorthand for an applyState trigger.

items.description: A stable identifier, unique within its collection. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore; must start with a letter or digit. Ids appear in saved runs, so renaming one breaks existing logs.

tags.description: Free tags, for cross-referencing and for filtering results out in some modes.

points.description: What a contestant earns for completing this result in a moderated mode. A result with points is a challenge the moderator can award; one without is an effect that lands on everyone.

needs.description: Requirements this result depends on, by id from the pack's `requires`. A run that said it lacks one of them draws again instead of landing here: a barbell movement for someone without a barbell, an oven dish in a kitchen without one.

items.description: A stable identifier, unique within its collection. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore; must start with a letter or digit. Ids appear in saved runs, so renaming one breaks existing logs.

prefixItems.description: Lowest roll that selects this entry, inclusive.
Highest roll that selects this entry, inclusive.

range.description: The inclusive roll range this entry owns. Across the table these must tile the dice range exactly, with no gaps and no overlaps.

items.description: One result in a lookup table.

entries.description: The results, each owning a span of the roll.

variants.description: The same table pitched more than one way, by a short name: `gentle`, `harsh`.

id.description: An SPDX identifier where there is one, else whatever name the terms go by.

redistributable.description: Whether somebody may pass this on.

description: Tables written once and used by any pack: the same set pitched several ways, so a pack can choose one and a run can choose another.

do.description: Roll dice and remember the total under a name.

into.description: Name to bind the total to, so a later branch can test it.

label.description: Shown to the player when prompting for the roll.

oneOf.description: Roll dice and remember the total under a name.

do.description: Roll on another table and resolve whatever comes up.

table.description: Id of the table to roll on.

times.description: How many times to roll. Defaults to 1.

timesFrom.description: Name a total bound earlier with `roll … into`; that many times, instead of `times`. How a pack rolls for how many to roll.

choose.description: With times > 1: `one` lets the player pick a single result to apply, `all` applies every result. Defaults to `all`.

into.description: Name to bind the rolled total to.

per.description: Who it is rolled for. `table` is the default and is the run's: one draw, everybody's. `contestant` draws once for each name on the roster and records each result against that name, so a watcher can see who got what and a replay gives it back. Only meaningful in a moderated mode, where there is a roster; elsewhere it is the run's as usual.

oneOf.description: Roll on another table and resolve whatever comes up.

do.description: Choose between action lists based on a value bound earlier.

on.description: Name of a value bound earlier by roll or prompt.

in.description: Match when the bound value is exactly one of these numbers.

is.description: Match when the bound value satisfies this comparison.

gte.description: Matches values greater than or equal to this.

lte.description: Matches values less than or equal to this.

gteCounter.description: Matches values greater than or equal to this counter's current value.

lteCounter.description: Matches values less than or equal to this counter's current value. This is what lets a roll be compared against something the run has accumulated, rather than a fixed number.

gteResource.description: Matches values greater than or equal to this resource's current value. The counter forms compare against what a run has accumulated; these compare against a dial somebody set, so a threshold can be the player's own answer to how often a thing should happen.

lteResource.description: Matches values less than or equal to this resource's current value.

gteFraction.description: Matches once the current unit has reached at least this fraction of the run's planned length, from 0 to 1. Needs the run to have said how long it is; a run that never did has no quarter to be in, so this never matches when `plannedUnits` is null or zero.

lteFraction.description: Matches while the current unit is still at most this fraction of the run's planned length, from 0 to 1. Same rule as `gteFraction`: no planned length, no match.

then.description: Actions to run when this case matches. The first matching case wins.

items.description: One arm of a branch. Provide either `in` for exact values or `is` for a range.

cases.description: Cases tested in order; the first match wins.

else.description: Actions to run when no case matches.

oneOf.description: Choose between action lists based on a value bound earlier.

do.description: Put a question to the player and remember the answer.

kind.description: What kind of answer is wanted: a subject, one of `options`, a state, a yes/no, or free text.

label.description: The question shown to the player.

into.description: Name to bind the answer to.

eligibleOnly.description: For kind `chooseSubject`: restrict the list to currently targetable subjects.

oneOf.description: Put a question to the player and remember the answer.

do.description: Pick which earlier subject a consequence lands on.

from.description: How to pick: `currentRoll` reads the roll that triggered this against the pack's targeting bands, `event` uses the fallback roll for consequences not tied to a band, `choice` lets the player decide.

into.description: Name to bind the chosen subject to. Also always available as targetSubject.

oneOf.description: Pick which earlier subject a consequence lands on, using the pack's targeting strategy. Required before any action that hits `targetSubject`.

state.description: Id of the declared state to attach.

label.description: How to describe the ban to the player.

oneOf.description: Forbid declaring further subjects of a given type for the rest of the run.

do.description: Queue mandatory extra units before the run may end.

count.description: How many extra units to queue. Defaults to 1.

oneOf.description: Queue mandatory extra units; the run cannot end while any remain.

do.description: Send the player back: when this unit closes, the run enters an earlier unit again instead of the next one.

count.description: How many units back. Defaults to 1: the previous unit is played again. Never before the first.

oneOf.description: Send the player back a unit or more, played again from its start, at the close of the current one.

do.description: Owe extra rolls on a table's step: the step is rolled again until they are paid.

table.description: Id of the table whose step rolls again.

count.description: How many extra rolls. Defaults to 1.

unit.description: Which unit owes them: `next` (the default) for "the next Stage rolls two Setbacks", `current` when the step has not happened yet this unit.

oneOf.description: Owe extra rolls on a table's step, this unit or the next; the flow keeps the step open until they are made.

do.description: Adjust a counter.

counter.description: Id of the counter to change.

setFrom.description: Set it to a value bound earlier, a roll's total or a prompt's answer, by name. Overrides `by` and `set`.

oneOf.description: Adjust a counter.

do.description: Adjust a resource.

resource.description: Id of the resource to change.

setFrom.description: Set it to a value bound earlier, a roll's total or a prompt's answer, by name. Overrides `by` and `set`.

oneOf.description: Adjust a resource, clamped to its declared min and max.

do.description: Draw cards into the player's hand.

deck.description: Id of the deck to draw from.

count.description: How many to draw. Defaults to 1.

oneOf.description: Draw cards into the player's hand.

do.description: Discard cards from hand without resolving them.

deck.description: Id of the deck the discarded card belongs to.

count.description: How many to discard. Defaults to 1.

oneOf.description: Discard cards from hand without resolving them.

do.description: Start a countdown the player must work against.

oneOf.description: Start a countdown the player must work against.

do.description: Give the player an instruction to carry out by hand.

text.description: The instruction shown to the player.

persistent.description: Keep it on screen for the rest of the run rather than clearing it once acknowledged.

oneOf.description: Give the player an instruction to carry out by hand, tracked as an obligation they tick off. Use this for anything the engine cannot do itself.

do.description: Set a boolean flag that predicates can later test.

value.description: Value to set. Defaults to true.

oneOf.description: Set a boolean flag that predicates can later test.

do.description: Try to end the run.

oneOf.description: Try to end the run. It may be refused, by queued forced units or by a trigger that fires on the attempt.

do.description: Run actions conditionally on run state.

then.description: Actions to run when the conditions hold.

else.description: Actions to run when they do not.

oneOf.description: Run actions conditionally on run state.

__schema0.description: One step of behavior. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: packs are data, never code.

ask.description: The yes/no question to put to the player, phrased so that yes means true.

anyOf.description: Ask the player. Use this for anything about the work itself, which the engine cannot inspect, whether a scene has dialogue, whether a track has effects, whether a lift felt heavy. Being honest about this is what keeps the format domain-agnostic.

lteFraction.description: Matches while the current unit is still at most this fraction of the run's planned length, from 0 to 1. Same rule as `gteFraction`: no planned length, no match.

unitIndex.description: A numeric comparison. Combine gte and lte for a closed range, or eq for an exact match. The `Counter` variants compare against a counter's current value instead of a literal, which is how a roll is measured against what the run has accumulated. The `Fraction` variants compare against how far into the run's planned length the current unit sits, which is what lets a pack say "the last quarter of the run" without knowing whether the run is six units or twenty.
